content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., after 79.68 or 82.31), then corrects with a downward bias.
- Underestimates in the middle-to-late horizon (days 15–30) when true values show upward momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: model assumes prices will return to prior levels faster than actual data shows.
- Lagged response: model reacts to recent history with delay — e.g., 79.58 → 80.41 is not captured until later in forecast.
- Avoids extreme outliers in history (e.g., 83.26) by underestimating their impact — model doesn’t “remember” or amplify spikes.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward higher values, suggesting model lacks downward correction mechanism after peaks.
